# A test fires the event of a component a loop inside a loop renders, where
# the inner loop walks what the outer one bound (`for var cell = row`). The
# handler reads the inner loop's variable, which the test's indices name as
# `cells[1][0]`; it read `row[0]`, which nothing in the test binds, and the Go
# targets failed to build on `undefined: row`.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +1 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component chip(label string, @tap()) ui.node {
    ui.button(text=label, @click { tap() })
}

// The inner loop walks what the outer one bound.
component grid(@open(name string)) ui.node {
    var cells = [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]

    ui.vbox {
        for var row = cells {
            ui.hbox {
                for var cell = row {
                    chip #step(label=cell, @tap { open(cell) })
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

component host ui.node {
    var opened = ""

    grid #g(@open(n) { opened = n })
}

func testTapOpensItsCell(t test.Test, c host) {
    c.g.step[1][0].tap()
    t.assert(c.opened == "c")
    c.g.step[0][1].tap()
    t.assert(c.opened == "b")
}

    }
  ]
}
